summary: A declared campaign against a problem turns into a named act and a new agency later that year.
realLife: Johnson declared war on poverty in his January 8, 1964 State of the Union. He signed the Economic Opportunity Act on August 20, 1964. It funded job training, community action programs and a youth volunteer effort.
sources: Read the State of the Union and the signing remarks.
inGame: The law engine's bill and agency rows, with the speech as the cause line.

turns.what: The declaration is followed by no bill that session.
turns.pulledBy: a legislature of the other party; an election year
turns.writesBack: The speech stays on the record with no later act.

turns.what: A smaller act passes with one program and no new agency.
turns.writesBack: The bill record lists the one program funded.
